bug_semantics: getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString applies /#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)/g to renderer-supplied Markdown when the Electron main process handles save and save-as. For an unmatched heading-like line such as '#' followed by a long run of spaces and then a newline, the greedy space quantifier and the two overlapping .* quantifiers around the required non-space character explore many equivalent partitions before failing. The synchronous match therefore grows approximately quadratically and blocks the Electron main process, freezing the application. In a direct Node probe, 1,000/2,000/4,000/8,000 spaces took 0.862/3.226/12.788/50.976 ms. The source-supported trigger is malicious document content followed by a save/save-as operation; the advisory's stronger remote/no-interaction characterization is not established by these call sites.
flaw_origin: Human-authored bug fix 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809 for #1281 changed the previously successful-on-spaces capture (.+) to the ambiguous failing capture (.*\S.*) in order to reject headings containing only spaces. That semantic change created the ReDoS failure path. The same patch was later replayed as dee8bb6f5b8a8e19a6e117f673c93f9dcad4aae1 on the release lineage; identical stable patch-id 6089600ebbeb76913148e7050d22a2ff06307ce0 shows that dee8bb6f is a backport/cherry-pick, not the original BIC.
ai_marker: No AI marker. `git cat-file -p 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809` shows author `Felix Häusler <hfelix@protonmail.ch>`, committer `Ran Luo <ransixi@gmail.com>`, and only the message `Fix recommend title exception when heading contains spaces only (#1281)`; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI-identifying trailers/identities in the BIC commit object.
evidence: In the validated clone, `git log -L 11,23:src/main/utils/index.js v0.17.1` attributes the vulnerable regex change directly to 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809 and shows its parent as 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7. `git log --all -S'#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)' -- src/main/utils/index.js packages/desktop/src/main/utils/index.ts` independently finds original 15f8c7b2, replay dee8bb6f, and only later TypeScript/monorepo moves.

`git diff 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809 -- src/main/utils/index.js` shows the single causal expression change from `(.+)` to `(.*\S.*)`. `git show 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7:src/main/utils/index.js` directly verifies that the parent contains only `markdown.match(/#{1,6} {1,}(.+)(?:\n|$)/g)` and lacks the vulnerable `.*\S.*` expression.

`git show 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809 | git patch-id --stable` and the same command for dee8bb6f5b8a8e19a6e117f673c93f9dcad4aae1 both produce patch-id 6089600ebbeb76913148e7050d22a2ff06307ce0. The original BIC has commit date 2019-08-19, whereas dee8bb6f was committed 2019-09-28; dee8bb6f is therefore the later replay that first put the flaw into the v0.15.1 release lineage, not a second root BIC.

Version boundary is reproducible with `git show v0.15.0:src/main/utils/index.js` (old `(.+)` expression) versus `git show v0.15.1:src/main/utils/index.js` (vulnerable `(.*\S.*)` expression). v0.17.1 still has it. `git grep -n '.*\\S.*' v0.19.1 -- '*utils/index*'`, `git show v0.20.0-rc.1:packages/desktop/src/main/utils/index.ts`, and `git show develop:packages/desktop/src/main/utils/index.ts` show it survived into v0.19.1, v0.20.0-rc.1, and clone head e52106fd1cdcbd33c1258b7b0cdc7013c4c5d86c. Thus the advisory's stated 'up to 0.17.1' ceiling is stale, not a fix boundary.

`git grep -n getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString v0.17.1 -- src` finds the function plus calls in `src/main/menu/actions/file.js` at the save and save-as handlers. Inspecting that blob around lines 100-115 and 230-246 shows synchronous evaluation of the renderer-supplied `markdown` before the save dialog, establishing the UI freeze path.

The advisory reproduction uses `'#' + ' '.repeat(100000) + '\n1\n'`. A bounded local Node probe of the exact vulnerable expression at 1,000, 2,000, 4,000, and 8,000 spaces measured 0.862, 3.226, 12.788, and 50.976 ms, approximately 4x time per 2x input. The proposed lookahead expression measured 0.058, 0.013, 0.022, 0.044, and 0.083 ms for 1,000 through 16,000 spaces.

GitHub PR API `https://api.github.com/repos/marktext/marktext/pulls/3952` reports state closed, `merged_at: null`, and `merge_commit_sha: null`. Its fork-only proposal c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560 changes the regex to include `(?! )`, as shown by `https://github.com/marktext/marktext/commit/c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560.patch`, but it never landed upstream. Therefore neither an upstream fix_sha nor an upstream direct_fix_sha exists.

`git cat-file -p 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809` is the BIC-only AI check: human author and committer identities, one ordinary 2019 bug-fix subject, and no trailers or AI/bot markers. No PR-body or later-commit signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior is specifically the unsuccessful spaces-only-heading match introduced when #1281 replaced (.+) with (.*\S.*). Line history, exact-string history, the parent diff, and the identical later backport patch establish 15f8c7b2 as the smallest original causal commit and directly establish parent absence. Its commit object has only human identities and no AI marker, so the causal code is NOT_AI. This attribution is closed even though remediation is not: PR #3952 supplied a plausible direct patch in a fork, but GitHub records it as closed and unmerged, while every later upstream release tag and current develop head inspected still carry the vulnerable expression.
remaining_gap: Upstream remains unpatched in the validated history through develop e52106fd1cdcbd33c1258b7b0cdc7013c4c5d86c; consequently there is no real upstream closing fix SHA or first fixed version to record. Fork proposal c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560 is not eligible as fix_sha/direct_fix_sha because PR #3952 was never merged.
